answer: Fieldwork attestation pins identity to ground. Each epoch the seed draws ten cells inside a miner's 25 km box, each with a landmark (a willow, a well head) and a beacon nailed to it. The miner gets six hours to photograph that cell, the epoch's word chalked on paper, EXIF intact, phone paired to the beacon, which answers only within ten meters. A cell clears once, so a thousand clones need a thousand people standing apart: eight dollars of wages and an hour of travel each, $8,000 a round, the map redrawn before any spot repeats. A pearl forms only around the grain an oyster holds.
